input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: Argument.get_help_record returns self.help unchanged, so the second element of the tuple is None for an undocumented argument even though format_arguments now feeds every record straight into formatter.write_dl without a fallback.
- failure path: A command declares two arguments and sets help on only one; running it with --help makes write_dl measure and wrap a None description and the help command crashes with a TypeError instead of printing usage.

Reviewer finding
- description: The positional-arguments section now passes every argument's help record straight to write_dl. For an argument with no help text, get_help_record now returns (metavar, None), so the description is None instead of the empty string the old fallback supplied.
- rationale: Trigger: a command with at least one positional argument that has help text and another positional argument with no help. The any() check passes, and write_dl receives a row whose second element is None. The width measurement in write_dl calls term_len on that value, which should raise TypeError. Impact: --help crashes for such commands instead of listing the arguments. This is a common command shape, so it is a crash on a common path.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label: get_help_record returns None for an undocumented argument, and format_arguments passes it to write_dl without a fallback. It also gives the same trigger, a mix of documented and undocumented arguments, and the same consequence, a TypeError when write_dl measures the None description.
